featured_findings.title: The ballot is mostly local, and much of it is fiscal.
featured_findings.deck: 89.3% of active records are local measures, and 55.7% fall into tax, bond, or spending-limit measure types.
featured_findings.method: Active, non-duplicate records grouped by county and consolidated measure type.
featured_findings.caveat: Measure type is more reliable than topic for CEDA-heavy local records.

featured_findings.title: Voters approve more measures than they reject.
featured_findings.deck: Among decided measures, 66.8% passed statewide and locally combined.
featured_findings.method: Decided active records where passed is coded 0 or 1.
featured_findings.caveat: This is descriptive, not a forecast for future measures.

featured_findings.title: Threshold rules create a class of majority-backed failures.
featured_findings.deck: 1,099 decided measures received more than 50% yes but did not pass, usually because a higher threshold applied.
featured_findings.method: Decided records with percent_yes above 50 and passed coded false.
featured_findings.caveat: A small number of threshold encodings are known to need manual verification.

featured_findings.title: Hundreds of measures are decided near the knife-edge.
featured_findings.deck: 2,149 measures landed within five percentage points of 50% yes.
featured_findings.method: Records with valid percent_yes and decided outcomes.
featured_findings.caveat: Margin is measured around 50%, not around each measure's legal passage threshold.

featured_findings.title: Measure activity is concentrated in the largest civic ecosystems.
featured_findings.deck: Los Angeles has the most local measures in the database, with 1,389 active records.
featured_findings.method: Active local records grouped by normalized county name.

featured_findings.title: Statewide proposition campaigns are often big-money contests.
featured_findings.deck: The finance database links 181 statewide proposition IDs and $5.8B in receipts.
featured_findings.caveat: Finance coverage is statewide-only and limited to matched proposition committees.

trend_insights.note: Trend lines are descriptive OLS fits over available records, not causal or coverage-adjusted estimates.

topic_trends.note: Topic trends exclude Other because sparse local topic text makes it a coverage artifact.

topic_insights.note: Era anchors and pass-rate rankings use the topic-classified subset (Other is excluded). Local CEDA records are better analyzed by measure type.

fiscal_instrument_profiles.typical_use: Borrowing for capital projects (schools, transit, infrastructure).
Local sales-tax surcharges for transit, public safety, or general fund.
Parcel and property taxes, often for schools or special districts.
Payroll, gross-receipts, or industry-specific business taxes.
Local levies on telecom, electricity, gas, or cable service.

type_insights.note: Modern-year anatomy uses records since 1990, where local category_type is consistently populated. Threshold profiles connect to the Rules panel for the deep dive.

statistical_comparisons.note: Odds ratios are descriptive associations from decided records and do not control for jurisdiction, year, topic, turnout, or selection into threshold rules.

marquee_fights.headline: App-based gig work vs labor
marquee_fights.takeaway: Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, and Instacart pooled into a single $81M Yes committee — five-to-one over the labor coalition opposing them. The measure passed.

marquee_fights.takeaway: The largest two-sided fight in the data ($181M). FanDuel and DraftKings spent $105M for; tribal coalitions led by San Manuel spent $76M against. Voters rejected it 17-83.

marquee_fights.title: Limiting Dialysis Revenue and Requiring Refund to Patients or Insurers Initiative
marquee_fights.headline: Dialysis profit caps vs the dialysis industry
marquee_fights.takeaway: DaVita and Fresenius spent $97M to defeat a SEIU-backed $24M effort to cap dialysis-clinic revenue. The industry side outspent the labor coalition about four-to-one — and won.

notes: CEDA dominates local measure coverage and is strongest for outcomes, categories, and vote totals.

Campaign finance analysis combines two year-scoped statewide proposition finance databases: v2 (finance_statewide_v2.db, monetary contributions) and v3 (finance_statewide_v3.db, loans + in-kind + independent expenditures). Scope: itemized monetary contributions to recipient committees tagged with each prop's CAL-ACCESS ballot number, plus loans (LOAN_CD), in-kind contributions (Form 460 Schedule C), and IE (Form 461 / 465 / S496) attributed to the measure via row-level fields, cover sheets, or curated overrides. Contributions to untagged side-committees and Schedule E party-passthroughs are still excluded. Our totals now approximate (but typically run somewhat below) press citations like Ballotpedia. Not available for local measures.
Pending-measure analogs are intentionally excluded from this MVP to avoid prediction framing.
